There is no existent thing. So how can time exist?"},"philosophy":{"insight":"The final argument: time depends on THINGS (events, phenomena, changes). But the MMK has already shown that things lack inherent existence (Chs.1-18). If the BASIS of time (things) is empty, then time itself must be empty. No inherent things → no inherent time. The emptiness of phenomena entails the emptiness of time.","madhyamaka":"Kāla bhāva-apekṣa (time depends on things). Bhāva-abhāve (in the absence of inherent things) kāla kutaḥ (whence time?). Na ca kaścid bhāvaḥ vidyate (no inherent thing exists — established in Chs.1-18). Tasmāt kāla katham bhaviṣyati (therefore, how could inherent time exist?). Time's emptiness follows from the emptiness of its basis.","quantum":"Relational time in physics: in general relativity, time is not a fixed background but is shaped by matter-energy (spacetime curvature). In loop quantum gravity, time emerges from physical processes. No matter/energy → no time. Like v.6: time depends on things; no inherent things → no inherent time.","bridge":"Both GR/LQG and v.6 show time depends on \"things\" (matter-energy / bhāva). GR: spacetime curvature depends on matter-energy distribution. V.6: time depends on phenomena. Both: remove the basis (matter / things), and time can't exist independently. Time is relational/dependent, not absolute.","accessible":"Without events (things happening), \"time\" means nothing. Time is measured BY events: heartbeats, clock ticks, planetary orbits. Take away all events, and there's no way to even define time. Time ISN'T a separate container — it's inseparable from the events within it.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: time and things exist together — events happen in time, and time is defined by events. Ultimately: both time and things lack inherent existence. Their mutual dependence is conventional, not inherent.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying time is created by material things. V.6 says time is CONCEPTUALLY DEPENDENT on things — it's defined relative to events. This is dependence, not creation. Time doesn't \"emerge\" from things; it's a conventional designation upon them."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Relational Time — Time Shaped by Matter-Energy","score":75,"strength":"High","explanation":"GR: spacetime curvature depends on matter-energy (no fixed background). The parallel is about time's non-independence from its basis."},"animation":{"visualBridge":"Events (objects, changes, processes) with time-arrows connecting them. Because things CHANGED: the clock shows a different time, the sun moved, your body rested. Without any change, you'd have no evidence of time passing. Time IS the pattern of changes."},{"q":"How does the MMK establish that \"no thing inherently exists\"?","a":"The entire MMK from Ch.1 to Ch.18: conditions are empty (Ch.1), motion is empty (Ch.2), perception is empty (Ch.3), aggregates are empty (Ch.4)... self is empty (Ch.18). V.6 builds on this cumulative result: no inherent things → no inherent time.","realLifeExample":"A building (time) rests on foundations (things). What makes Ch.19 especially striking is its resonance with contemporary physics: general relativity (time shaped by matter), loop quantum gravity (time emergent from processes), and the Wheeler-DeWitt equation (fundamental timelessness).
